before:
São Paulo's city airport, 8 km from downtown in Campo Belo, and second busiest in Brazil after Guarulhos. For a client staying in the city this is by far the most convenient of São Paulo's four commercial airports.

Capacity is deliberately capped. Congonhas is slot restricted to a maximum of 30 operations an hour, one of only five airports in Brazil with such limits, so availability is tighter than the traffic figures suggest.

Getting between airports is well organised. A monorail station sits next to the terminal. Azul runs free transfers to Campinas-Viracopos for its own passengers, and Gol and TAM do the same to Guarulhos. There is also an executive bus line between Guarulhos and Congonhas calling at Tietê bus terminal, Barra Funda, Itaim Bibi, Praça da República and the hotels along Avenida Paulista, taking about an hour depending on traffic.

The airport was planned in 1919 and opened in April 1936. It was officially renamed after Deputy José Freitas Nobre in 2017, but everyone still says Congonhas.
after:
São Paulo's city airport, about 9 km from the centre in Campo Belo. It is Brazil's second busiest after Guarulhos, with 24.5 million passengers in 2025. Its scheduled flights are all domestic, mainly with LATAM, Gol and Azul. For a client staying in the city it is the most convenient of São Paulo's airports. Aena, which won a 30-year concession in 2022, runs it.

Capacity is deliberately capped. Congonhas is one of four Brazilian airports where ANAC, the regulator, allocates take-off and landing slots. Regular flights are not allowed after 11pm.

The Airport Bus Service runs executive coaches between Congonhas and Guarulhos airport. A monorail to the airport, Line 17-Gold, was still under construction in August 2026, according to the city's Metrô.

The airport opened in 1936. It was officially renamed after Deputy Freitas Nobre in 2017, but it is still known as Congonhas.

claims.inAfter: Congonhas is one of four Brazilian airports where ANAC, the regulator, allocates take-off and landing slots
claims.note: Was 'slot restricted to a maximum of 30 operations an hour, one of only five airports in Brazil with such limits'. ANAC coordinates four airports today (Congonhas, Guarulhos, Recife, Santos Dumont); DECEA's live entry also calls Congonhas a coordinated aerodrome. The count of four is ANAC's own, so the sentence names ANAC.

claims.inAfter: Regular flights are not allowed after 11pm.
claims.note: New, in place of the 30-an-hour cap, which no current source gives. ANAC (9 September 2026): Resolution 55/2008 bars regular commercial and general aviation operations after 23:00; a new exception only lets flights already scheduled that day finish after 23:00 in emergencies such as bad weather. DECEA requires prior permission for any operation between 02:00 and 09:00 UTC, which is 23:00 to 06:00 local time (UTC-3). Wikipedia's 22:30 closing is out of date.
